caption: Opening page of 'The Second Day of the Feast: Natéma Umártinyu' in Karsten's 1923 Bureau of American Ethnology bulletin.
alt: Printed page 70 headed 'The Second Day of the Feast: Natéma Umártinyu, "The Drinking of the Natéma"', beginning the account of the natéma (ayahuasca) drinking ceremony among the Jíbaro.
credit: Internet Archive / Rafael Karsten, Blood Revenge, War, and Victory Feasts among the Jibaro Indians of Eastern Ecuador, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 79 (Washington: GPO, 1923), p. 70
note: This is the section's opening text page, not an illustrated plate: the bulletin's photographic plates (of Jíbaro house life, warriors, and the tsantsa-washing ceremony) fall at pages 62 and 78, on either side of the natéma section, but none depicts the natéma drinking itself, so the section's own title page was used instead.
